utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. No preliminaries; therefore, we can immediately start to hear the next witness's evidence. The next witness will give its testimony through videolink. Therefore, the first thing we have to do is to establish whether the videolink is functioning well. I already see the representative of the Registry at the other side of the videolink. Could you confirm that you can hear us and that you can see us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes. Good morning, Your Honours. We can see and hear you clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We can see and hear you clearly as well. Mr. Lukic, is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honour. We are calling Mr. Bosko Kelecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom at the other side of the videolink. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to put on the record, it's the Prosecution's position that the witness should be advised of his rights pursuant to the Rule 90(E). I understand Mr. Lukic takes his standard objection to doing so, and I just wanted to raise it for the Chamber. I know sometimes it's been done at the beginning and sometimes at the beginning of cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's do it the following way. If Mr. Lukic has no questions which would require such a warning, then we'll do it at the beginning of the examination by the party that thinks that there is a need to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Before I invite the witness to make the solemn declaration, could the representative of the Registry tell the Chamber who are in the videolink room?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Beside myself, it's the witness and the ICTY technician.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr. Kelecevic. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration of which the text, as I can see, has been handed out to you already, may I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good morning. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Kelecevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kelecevic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General. I can't hear you. Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, would you kindly tell me, slowly, your full name.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Bosko Kelecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kelecevic, did there come a time when you gave a written statement to the Defence team of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I did give one statement. It was at the offices of the Tribunal. I think it was the month of December 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But my question was whether you have given a statement to the Defence team of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: No, I have never had any contact with them. Oh, you mean now? Yes, yes. I meant in 2001. Yes, I have given a written statement that I signed in my own hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll now look at a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D1731.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see you have it on paper in front of you. Let's wait until we have it here on the screen in the courtroom. On page 1, General, do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose is it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's see the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see a signature there? Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose is it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General Kelecevic, did you have occasion to look through this statement and is everything that you've said to the Defence team of General Mladic recorded accurately?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Everything is accurate, as I've read it and signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it truthful, what you've read in the statement that you've signed?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, it's truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to ask you the same questions today, would you give essentially the same answers?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: The same answers, maybe. Not exactly the same words but the essence would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We should like to tender General Kelecevic's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be assigned Exhibit number D1110. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1110 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General Kelecevic, thank you. At this moment, we have no questions for you. And we are not going to read the brief summary of the witness's statement, because we'll hear everything through the cross-examination and the public will be well informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether the cross-examination will seek to have the witness repeat all what he said in his statement, so you can't rely on that. And if it's not yet prepared, I would nevertheless invite you to read the short summary then soon. But if you have one, please read it out now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll just mention the topics that General Kelecevic will testify to. He speaks, first of all, about his career, the outbreak of the war in Slovenia and in Croatia. Then he's transferred to Bosnia and Herzegovina, first to Sarajevo, then to Banja Luka, the then 5th Corps, where he was appointed chief of staff of the 5th Corps. He later became chief of staff of the 1st Corps of Republika Srpska. General Kelecevic also talked to us about the Operation Corridor in which he was actively involved beginning with the first operations. He also speaks about the events in Prijedor to the extent of his knowledge, and what he knows about the operation and the closing down of the Manjaca camp. That would be briefly the extent of Mr. Kelecevic's written testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Lukic. Perhaps unnecessary to say this, but often in the statement we do not find a clear source of knowledge. Sometimes the evidence also is, to some extent, repetitious. But, for example, the Hambarine incident, he says how it was, where he was, how he learned about that, that's all unknown, but perhaps during cross-examination that may become clear. Mr. Traldi, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I am, though I'd ask that the Chamber give the witness the advice we discussed earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the Prosecution specifically invited me, and that's what I'm doing now, to inform you about the content of Rule 90(E) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I'll just read it to you. 90(E) reads: "A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." That means that if you fear that a truthful answer might tend to incriminate yourself, please address me and ask to be relieved from your duty to answer that question. The Chamber will then decide how we will proceed. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. You'll soon see him on your screen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, as you mentioned earlier, you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor in 2001 as a suspect. Is it your position that you told the truth at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, at that time I was not a suspect. I told the whole truth. It's true that it was in 2001. I did not receive any minutes of that to remind myself of what exactly I talked about in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We may have occasion to see some examples over the next couple of days. But before we do, could we have 65 ter 32812.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps I add at this moment, Mr. Kelecevic, whether you are considered to be a suspect or not has some legal consequences, and the Prosecution apparently - unless you made a mistake, Mr. Traldi - the Prosecution apparently interviewed you as a suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll check and I'll report to the Chamber at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll later hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if I can help. I just checked electronically that interview, and I don't see where it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi said he would come back to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I appreciate Mr. Lukic's assistance, as always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is a selection of excerpts from your personnel file from the FRY Secretariat of National Defence. Turning to page 19 in the English, and 12 in the B/C/S, we see your assessment from General Talic for the period 12 March 1992 to 12 March 1996. In the middle of the page in the English and at the top of the page in the B/C/S, we see the grade 5.00. That's the highest possible grade; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Mr. Traldi, you need to bear with me for a minute. The document takes a while to open. Could you direct me to the B/C/S page number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Page 12 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the numerical grade is at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] You can proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think, General, you've confirmed that's the highest possible grade, 5.0.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn now to page 21 in the English and 13 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what we see here is General Talic's descriptive grade. He writes that you carry out the duty of chief of staff of the corps very successfully and that you planned and directly controlled the corridor operation. And we see at the bottom you're awarded the favourable grade of "excellent." Now, this reflects General Talic's approval of your work as chief of staff of the 1st Krajina Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Correct. But if you allow me, I would like to say -- sorry, you wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If you have an additional comment about this assessment, sir, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: No, I have no comments about the assessment of General Talic, but all my previous assessments, beginning with 1965, all of them were with distinction. It's not only the assessment of General Talic. I met him for the first time in 1993, in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were interpreted to say 1993, sir. Just for the transcript, I'm sure you meant to say 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 27 in the B/C/S and 41 in the English, and here we see General Mladic's proposal for a promotion for you dated the 14th of October, 1993. Now, this is a proposal that's being made to the VJ; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it's not 1993. It's 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, we see the date clearly marked 14 October 1993 in the top left. You were also promoted in the VRS in 1992 after Operation Corridor; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turn to page 42 in the English and the third-to-last paragraph on page 27 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this the same document? You introduced it earlier when the other page was on our screen as a proposal for a promotion. We didn't look at -- we still have the original on our left screen, 14th of October. Is that the one you're referring to? Because it looks to me that if there is another name under it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. I am afraid I don't entirely understand what I'm being asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You introduced the document as a -- and it is the document which is on the left of my screen at this moment. Oh, no. I see that I'm reading it wrongly. Yes. No, it's fine. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In the third-to-last paragraph of the document, we see General Mladic assesses that you could be very much credited for strengthening command and control in the KK, which is secured through efficient engagement and steering of the staff organs, as well as lower formations on realisation of the commander's decision. Now, this describes your role as chief of staff of the 1st Krajina Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But, Your Honours, I would like to see a few words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to be more specific. In the 5th Military District in Zagreb -- yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the question was whether this describes your role as chief of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please not interrupt me. The question was whether -- what was read to you, whether that describes your role as chief of staff. Now, if you have a matter which is directly linked to that question, you may raise it. If it is not directly linked to that question, you should wait for the next question to be put to you. So what you intended to say, is that directly related to the question? Then please proceed. Otherwise, wait for the next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it is related to my promotion. I wanted to say that I was made general back in 1988 by a decree made already in Zagreb in the 5th Military District.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It may be related to your promotion. It was not related to the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- from Zagreb you were sent to the 2nd Military District when it was formed; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I was not sent there. In reality, I was thrown out because it was the way the role of the command of the 5th Military District via Zagreb through Croatia to Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we didn't go straight to Sarajevo but it went gradually through Plitvice, Slunj, Bihac, Kozara, up to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to interrupt you --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: This withdrawal, this retreat lasted four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you to focus on my question. Is it correct that beginning on the 10th of January, 1992 when the 2nd Military District of the JNA was formed, you held the position of chief of security there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Right. It was not on the 10th but the 1st of January, 1992. I arrived in Sarajevo on the 7th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the JNA corps that comprised the 2nd Military District all became part of the VRS in May 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender 65 ter 32812. This includes about 20 per cent of the personnel file, and we've uploaded the portions that we consider relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, there are no other portions you would consider to be added?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have the document yet with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We have disclosed the full version, and, as always, if there are additional parts that Mr. Lukic would want admitted in context, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you always can revisit the matter, if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit number P7458. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7458 is admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, at page 12, line 8 -- I'm sorry. Line 15. I thought I heard you mention the month in 1992 when the 2nd Military District became part of the VRS, but it's not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd referred to the month of May, Your Honour. And thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32720.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a page out of Glas from the 22nd of March 1992 and to the lower right-hand side of the page in black, we see an article entitled "New Commandant." And it says, it reports that you have taken the position of chief of staff of the 5th Corps, it refers to the Banja Luka Corps, and the duty of commandant of the Corps has been assumed by the previous chief of staff, General Talic. And it describes this at the beginning of the article as "in the spirit of the general transformation in the JNA." Now, from this point, you were chief of staff for the rest of the war, first of the 5th Corps and then of the 1st Krajina Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: At the time, if it is late March, it is correct then that I was chief of staff as of the 15th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you remained chief of staff, first of the JNA 5th Corps and then of the VRS 1st Krajina Corps, throughout the remainder of the war; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: The 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then of the VRS 1st Krajina Corps. And you held those positions throughout the war; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Correct. As of the 12th of May, 1992 until the end of the war, I remained the chief of staff of the 1st Corps in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And General Talic remained your immediate superior from the 15th of March when you were appointed chief of staff of the 5th Corps through the end of the war, including your service in the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And General Talic was a hands-on commander; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Am I supposed to answer that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You are.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Talic has exercised almost all command duties throughout his career, and he was a very good hands-on commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And responsibility for what the corps does, all its actions, always lies with the commander; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: The commander is always responsible, irrespective of whether he is at the command post, in the movement, or stationary, if he's within the area of responsibility of his unit. In his absence, the deputy commander stands in, the person being the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If you stood in for General Talic, when he came back he wouldn't say: General Kelecevic, don't tell me anything about what happened while I was gone. That's not my problem. That's not my responsibility; would he?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We have technical problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have -- one second, please. We have an audio problem at this moment. Mr. Registrar, could you say a few lines so that we see whether the audio is now better or rather hear, hear whether it's any better.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Test 1, 2, 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. 4, 5, 6 would follow, I think. It seems that it has been repaired or is functioning now well again. Witness, did you hear the question well that was put to you by Mr. Traldi; that is, what General Talic would not say if he --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be repeated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If you stood in for General Talic, when he came back he wouldn't say: General Kelecevic, don't tell me anything about what happened while I was gone. That's not my problem. That's not my responsibility; would he?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: He would never say that. And I would not allow myself to fail him to acquaint with the situation during his absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if he issued an order and then left the command post, he would expect you to continue to oversee the continued implementation of that order; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Right. The commander's order must always be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the 5th Corps of the JNA was part of the 2nd Military District; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was part of the 2nd Military District until the 12th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when you arrived at the 5th Corps, General Kukanjac was General Talic's immediate superior; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Not his immediate superior because at the time General Vukovic commanded the corps. Chief of staff was General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Beginning just a couple of days after you arrived in Banja Luka when General Talic formally assumed the duty of commander of the 5th Corps, General Kukanjac was his immediate superior; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And beginning on the 10th of May, 1992 when General Mladic became commander of the JNA 2nd Military District carrying through until 1996 when he handed over his command, he was General Talic's immediate superior; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: We take it to be the 12th of May rather than the 10th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P7459. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7459 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, we may or may not discuss the 10th and 11th of May later during your testimony, but I take it you agree that from the 12th of May through the rest of the war and continuing to 1996, General Mladic was General Talic's immediate superior; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, could we have Exhibit P431, page 41 in the English, 34 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this will be the transcript of the 16th Session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly, held on the 12th of May, 1992. This session was held in the JNA hall in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I was informed through the media. I was not present at the session. I only know about it through the media. I know that it was held and I learned of its conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say you learned of its conclusions, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that on the 12th of May, the Republika Srpska was established. It was a decision by the assembly to establish Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, Republika Srpska had been declared in January 1992, hadn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And General Mladic was placed in command of it; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One of the other things that was decided at this assembly was the strategic objectives of the Bosnian Serb people; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose it was the case and that they were proclaimed concerning the defence of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you also learned about those; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: How did you learn about them?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: First and foremost, I learned about it from the commander who informed his ranks; and secondly, I learned about it through the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say the commander informed his ranks, do you mean General Talic?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't say that it was Talic personally, but I can suppose it was done by his assistant for political affairs who, at the time, I think, was Colonel Vukelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall when and where he informed you of these objectives?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I can't recall. No way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, returning to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know where and when. Do you know how you were informed? Was it in a written form or was it in a conversation or in a meeting? Do you have any recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that information was always sent to the units when it came to something that important. So written information was sent to the units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that your reconstruction or is it your recollection that it happened this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would rather say that I'm trying to reconstruct. I can't say positively that things developed that way. I'm just relying on what was usually done under such circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the objectives that you learned of, those included - most importantly for the 1st Krajina Corps - separation from Muslims and Croats and the establishment of a corridor connecting the Bosnian Krajina with the eastern part of Republika Srpska through the Posavina region; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: That was the task, but I wouldn't say that we had to establish a corridor. It was already in existence and it had not been cut off at the time. It will become cut off at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When was it cut off?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: The corridor was cut off -- well, since I was in the area and I had been tasked with deployment and assessment of the situation, I can tell you that the corridor was cut off three times in late March, in early June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, here we see a portion of General Mladic's speech at the 16th assembly, and in the middle of the page in English I'm simply going to read you what he says. He's describing the army and he says: "We are not starting from scratch. That is very important. Our starting point are the armed Serbian people in the Republika Srpska of Bosnia and Herzegovina, who have, in the course of the war so far, responded, insofar as they did, to the call to put a stop, together with the members of the Yugoslav Peoples' Army, to the fascist and phantom Ustasha dragon. And so far, we have saved this people from being totally wiped out." Now, when General Mladic says "we are not starting from scratch," he's referring to the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: He is probably discussing - if this is May, because I did not pick up the date, perhaps you can remind me. But I don't know the date of this intervention of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the date is still the 12th of May, 1992 at the 16th assembly. General Mladic is talking about the army and he says: "We are not starting from scratch." He says, "our starting point are the armed Serbian people." He mentions what they have already been doing together with the members of the Yugoslav Peoples' Army. So what I'm putting to you is that when General Mladic says "we are not starting from a scratch," what he's saying is the VRS is not starting from scratch. It's starting from the armed Serbian people who have been operating together with members of the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, if this was at the 16th Session and if Mr. Mladic said that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We need to stop for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. One second. For how long would you have to stop?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness should repeat the entirety of his answer because the sound was simply too poor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you restart your answer. You started by saying: "Well, you see, if this was at the 16th Session and if Mr. Mladic said that ..." Could you resume from there what you said? Because the sound was poor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Mladic said this on the 12th at the 16th assembly session. Until the 12th of May, the 2nd Military District was still in existence and operational, and of course it is normal that he said that we were not starting from scratch. If you take the 5th Corps alone, it basically continued its activities and tasks it had previously had, even back in January 1992, when the 2nd Military District was established. I think I'm sufficiently clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the weapons and personnel of the 5th Corps remained in Bosnia and transformed into the 1st Krajina Corps of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you think that the 5th Corps had not had its weapons before that date? It had the weapons in the 2nd Military District and the same weapons remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: General Kelecevic, before we move on from this document, what is a fascist and phantom Ustasha dragon?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say because I don't ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I think your answer may have been cut off. You said you don't and then I imagine you were going to explain what you don't do.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say what the meaning is, this Ustasha dragon. I never used such terms and I didn't want to hear about it. On the other hand, I'm quite knowledgeable when it comes to fascism.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Why didn't you want to hear about such terms?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I think it wasn't part of our jargon, this fascist dragon. As for the term "dragon" itself, it would imply that it is extremely dangerous. I think fascism is a very dangerous thing for the human kind in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's inflammatory language, obviously; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it's inflammatory, but it definitely is not something pleasant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I think Judge Moloto had a question for you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Actually for you, Mr. Traldi. Mr. Traldi, you asked the witness if by referring to "we are not starting afresh," General Mladic was referring to the VRS. I just wanted to find out whether the answer at page 21, lines 2 to 8, answers your question and are you happy that your question has been answered?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was satisfied with the answer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, we have just a few minutes before the break. In that time, I'm going to just try to nail down some of the key players in the 1st Krajina Corps besides you and General Talic. At the beginning of the war, the assistant commander for security and intelligence was Colonel Stevilovic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand. Colonel who?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Stevilovic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Stevilovic. I know him. He was my subordinate organ in the 5th Military District in the security organ in Maribor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he was killed in July 1992 and replaced by Stevan Bogojevic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't replaced by Stevan. He was replaced by Stevo Bogojevic who unfortunately passed away some two months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that the political officer was Milutin Vukelic. Had he held that position in the 5th Corps previously?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: He did not hold the same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The 5th Corps --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: The -- excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The 5th Corps's political officer had been a Colonel Mesud Hasotic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: It was Colonel Hasotic, but I can't say precisely when he left that position. Colonel Milutin Vukelic came in his stead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Hasotic was a Muslim; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you be careful in pronouncing the names, because if you are talking too fast it is not properly recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I will try, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The assistant commander for logistics was Colonel Vaso Tepsic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I'm looking at the clock. If it is a matter of one or two names, then please proceed. Otherwise, we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's more like three or four and so I'll suggest we take the break, if it's agreeable to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Mr. Kelecevic, we'll take a break of 20 minutes. We'd like to see you back at 10 minutes to 11.00, because we'll resume at ten to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, you're supposed not to speak aloud. Last warning. Could we check whether the videolink is still functioning well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour. We can see and hear you clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can see and hear you as well. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to get back to the Chamber about the matter Mr. Lukic raised at the beginning of cross-examination. He's quite correct, as often, that in this case General Kelecevic was interviewed pursuant to a summons but not as a suspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- yes. So therefore a mistake on your side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, when we'd left off, we'd confirmed that the 1st Krajina Corps's assistant commander for logistics was General Tepsic. Had he held the same position in the 5th Corps of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was also in the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to focus on my question. Had he held --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There is something wrong with the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to focus on my question. Had he held the same position - that is, assistant commander for logistics - in the 5th Corps of the JNA before the transformation?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: He was assistant commander for logistics in the 5th Corps all the way until the moment when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, from May 1992 until he was killed in 1993, he was the assistant commander for logistics in the 1st Krajina Corps of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Right. He wasn't killed exactly in the sense of assassinated. He got killed in a car accident.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he was replaced by Bosko Amidzic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Colonel Amidzic, Bosko.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the 1st Krajina Corps's assistant commander for civilian affairs was Colonel Gojko Vujinovic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: No, Vujinovic. Gojko Vujinovic, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Gojko Vujinovic was the 1st Krajina Corps's assistant commander for civilian affairs; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what was Dragan Marcetic's position?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Marcetic was assistant chief of staff for operations and training in the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Zdravko Djuric's position?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Not Ceric but Djuric, Zdravko. Zdravko Djuric was assistant chief of staff for intelligence. The intelligence and security were separate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you check the spelling of the name in page 25, line 23. Dragan and then the family name. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No. And thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The assistant chief of staff for operations and training, that was Dragan Marcetic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Correct. Not assistant commander but assistant chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And these two men whose positions you've described as assistant chief of staff, Marcetic and Djuric, who was their immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Their immediate superior was the chief of staff; that is to say, myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we mentioned Colonel Vujinovic a moment ago. One of his responsibilities was maintaining contact between the 1st Krajina Corps and the regional Crisis Staff; right? The ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Not only the Crisis Staff but all the civilian affairs in the area of responsibility of this corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: That was Gojko Vujinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you're explaining, I take it, and correct me if I'm wrong, that he was responsible for maintaining contact with the regional Crisis Staff, the ARK Crisis Staff, but also with municipal civilian authorities; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Correct. With the civilian authorities in the area of responsibility of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Colonel Bogojevic, the assistant commander for security and intelligence, would always maintain contacts with the civilian police, the MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Not Blagojevic. Bogojevic, Stevo. He was assistant for security. Not intelligence. Intelligence was the domain of Djuric. There were two separate jobs. Security and intelligence were separate in the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me try and ask the question again very specifically. Colonel Bogojevic, who you've just described, would always maintain contact with the civilian police, the MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: The civilian police, and of course he was the superior of the military police, professionally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So that's yes, he would always maintain contact with the civilian police; right? I ask you to just give a "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, there were also two units in Banja Luka that were under the direct control of the VRS Main Staff, the 14th Logistics Base and the 89th Rocket Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Plus there was airforce and anti-aircraft defence of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the head of the airforce, General Ninkovic, he was based in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Ninkovic is the correct last name. Ninkovic and his command were in Banja Luka in the garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And there was an airforce squadron at a place called Mahovljani, M-a-h-o-v-l-j-a-n-i; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's part of the airforce. The airfield was called Mahovljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Its commander was Zoran Jokic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I know him only by name. I've never seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But you know he was the commander of that squadron; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: No. If you mean the airforce, there is airforce and the anti-aircraft defence; that is to say, the anti-aircraft rocket system.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I mean the Mahovljani squadron based at the place we've just been discussing. Zoran Jokic was the commander of that squadron; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't find Jokic there when I arrived. He was part of the airforce and anti-aircraft defence. He must have been there in March. Later, he was replaced by Colonel Bozo Novak who later became a general.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you've provided a lot of information. None of it responsive to my question. The position he held in which he was replaced was commander of that airforce squadron at Mahovljani; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that. You didn't tell me the exact unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Jokic, like General Talic, was a member of the ARK Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I know that Talic was on the list of the Crisis Staff. About Jokic, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, how often in 1992 - how regularly - would General Talic hold morning meetings of his assistant commanders?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: These meetings of the commander with the collegium were regular, but not like in peacetime because the front line was very, very broad, so only the inner core of the command would meet. And the other organs of the staff would come less frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The inner core included the assistant commanders that we've discussed this morning; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. These assistant commanders, the chief of staff, the assistant for logistics, for security, for civilian affairs, they would meet almost every week once a week unless there was some extraordinary situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And on days that there wasn't a meeting, General Talic would have contact by phone with the assistant commanders; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He would also, after speaking with them, have contact by phone with General Mladic; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, in these contacts he would report about the situation in the unit; although, there were always regular combat reports delivered at a certain time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the way it worked, in fact, is the regular combat report would be sent from the corps to the Main Staff based on information provided by the corps's subordinate units, and then General Talic would speak with General Mladic so they could follow-up on any issues included in the regular combat report; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, essentially, yes. But it doesn't mean that they talked every day. They talked if they had something to discuss, a problem to solve, then they would get in touch. If something has been covered in a report and no additional explanation was needed, they didn't necessarily talk about it. It was not something that had to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we've reviewed a number of the duty log-books from the corps during that period, and, sir, setting whether it happened every day aside, General Talic very regularly spoke by phone with General Mladic after the daily combat report was sent, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Not necessarily. If something has been sent in encrypted form, it's not discussed over communication means. But certainly when they met, they discussed certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, in General Talic's absence, you would speak by phone with General Mladic about what was going on in the corps's area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Unless it was sent in a written report and something needed to be reported or said, I would then do it if the commander was not at his place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Main Staff would issue orders and directives to the 1st Krajina Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: General Talic together with you and the rest of the corps command staff would turn those into operational orders for the corps's subordinate units; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: If it was necessary for the subordinated units to be informed and given orders, that was always done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And General Mladic and other Main Staff officers would also visit the 1st Krajina Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When General Mladic came to the 1st Krajina Corps's area of responsibility, how would you be informed he was coming?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, sometimes I was informed. Sometimes I was not informed. Sometimes he would come unannounced.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Would he bring a detail, a security detail, with him?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Of course he had a security detail. And he brought them not to the commander -- not to the meetings with the commander but when he was travelling in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So if he were to visit units in the field, his detail would go with him?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you'd be aware of where he was going as long as he was in your area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes I would know in advance, but sometimes he wouldn't tell me. He had the right to tour and to make inspections and visit places he considered he wanted to visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Stepping back to March 1992 for a moment. At the time you took over your position as chief of staff, a number of 5th Corps units were deployed in Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And shortly after you arrived in Banja Luka, many of those units were redeployed back from Croatia to the Bosnian Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: This is not such an easy question to answer. I can either give you a broader answer or not say anything. The units of the corps went out there in August 1991 across the Sava River to the area of Slavonia where Serbs were living, and they went there to protect the Serbian people. They stayed in Slavonia until 15 of June when that area was taken over by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in fact, the 122nd Brigade was deployed back to Kotor Varos and Travnik in March of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you exactly when. It was 20 years ago. It was a period when I was still in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the 6th Brigade was deployed back to Sanski Most at the beginning of April when you were in the 5th Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: If you mean the calendar year, that's right. But you have to understand that this area of responsibility comprises 28 municipalities. It had a 260-kilometre long front line. I could not cover physically all the units and all the sectors. Whether it was exactly that number of the unit you mentioned, I can't be sure now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So we saw your assessment earlier. An excellent chief of staff doesn't need to know where his subordinate brigades are, what republic they're in?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: That's not what I'm trying to say. It's true the chief of staff has to know the location of his units. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you apparently ignored that the witness said "I can't be sure now," whereas in your follow-up question you suggested that he didn't know at the time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the time, sir, you surely knew when the 6th Brigade was redeployed from Croatia back to Sanski Most; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time I probably knew from the reports. But I'm now talking to you specifically about myself as the chief of staff. On the 28th of April, I left the command post and went to a completely different area from which I supervised a completely different situation and later on that would evolve into the issue of the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you give some evidence about operations in Prijedor in May 1992 in your statement. Is it your position that you don't have any personal knowledge about those operations because you were in a completely different area?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not saying I don't know anything. I said I did not personally control these operations. I was not there. Specifically, that 43rd Motorised Unit from Prijedor was still across the river Sava over there in Croatia in Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, by late May 1992, the 43rd Brigade was in Prijedor, just like the 6th Brigade was in Sanski Most; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: No, you can't say that about the whole of the brigade. Perhaps one part of it was. But the command, let's say the 43rd, I know about them for sure, the command of the 43rd Brigade was still in Slavonia in Croatia. As far as the 6th Brigade is concerned, I cannot say with certainty whether it had returned already to Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, earlier you said when asked about the 6th Brigade returning to Sanski Most, as part of your answer you said: "On the 28th of April, I left the command post and went to a completely different area from which I supervised a completely different situation." But the question about the return of the 6th Brigade to Sanski Most was not about something that happened after the 28th of April but, as Mr. Traldi put it to you, was early April. So I have difficulties in understanding why your departure on the 28th of April may have any impact on your knowledge in early April.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's 13 days after I came to become the chief of staff. For 13 days - that is to say, from the 17th of March until the beginning of April - that's 13 days. That's how much time I spent in the area. Was I able to take stock of all of that at once? I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That may be an explanation but it's a different one from the previous one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, we'll talk about several of these units in detail later. The reason 5th Corps units were deployed back to Bosnia, they were deployed back to take control of the territory and the situation in the Bosnian Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: What is your question, precisely?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 5th Corps units were deployed back to Bosnia to take control of the territory and the situation in the Bosnian Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I said that the units of both the 1st and the 5th Corps, because it was a period of overlap and there was the issue of whether they were in the military district or in the VRS in the month of May. In any case, the corps units remain in Slavonia - i.e., in Croatia - until the 15th of June, 1992. That part. Not all of the units but some units of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's first have 65 ter 32715, page 36. And, sir, this will be part of your OTP interview which you testified earlier had been truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I've got the wrong page number, so I'll move on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: By the time these units were redeployed, and I'll continue suggesting that it was long before the 15th of June for most of them, these were battle-tested units with experience at the front in Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: It was the case with some units but not with others. I don't know what particular unit you are interested and whether it was part of the 1st or the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, all the brigades we just mentioned - the 122nd, the 6th, the 343rd - those were battle-tested units with experience at the front in Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. The units that had been in the territory of Slavonia had been battle-tested.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that included the three units I just referred to; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 6th and the 43rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have 65 ter 32715, page 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This, again, is your OTP interview. The bottom of the page you're asked about the 122nd Brigade withdrawing from Croatia to Bosnia in March, and you answer, you explain there was a danger of escalation occurring. You're asked: "Which is why units were withdrawn into these areas to actually take control of the territory and the situation?" And you answer: "Of course it was the reason. I mean, all the men fit for service, because Croats and Muslims would not go into, into their units, so all the men fit for service in that, in that entire area were in Slavonia, so there was absolutely no one to defend this, this population." And then you're asked: "And the Muslims and Croats in this entire area were seen as the threat that needed to be controlled by the deployment of these forces into this area, weren't they?" And you answer: "Of course. It wasn't the Hungarians or the, the Romanians or the Bulgarians that were, that were the problem. It was, it was them." Do you stand by the portions of your OTP interview that I've just read back to you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I can't recall whether I put it in those very words but I stand by the fact that the units, which had been in Croatia, in Slavonia, that sizable chunks of those units returned to the area to protect and to separate the forces there and calm the situation down in Prijedor and Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To take control of the situation and to take control of the threat posed by the Muslims and Croats. Those are the propositions you confirmed in your interview. Do you stand by that today, "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I stand by it today because in a certain period on certain days the Muslim and Croat forces carried out certain attacks on military facilities, units, and columns along those axes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, those 5th Corps units that were deployed back to the Bosnian Krajina, they were supplemented by mobilised Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. They were also being manned with Muslim and Croat conscripts who were assigned to the units. Those who had given their oath and agreed to fighting with the unit were recruited. Those who refused were considered deserters because they did not want to be included in the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did that oath involve protecting the Serb people, the Serb authorities that had been established?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it certainly included the institutions, the people, and the Serb institutions that existed at the time but also the Muslims and Croats who resided in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to look at the mechanics of that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P3032.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an order issued by General Mladic on the 11th of May, 1992 from the 2nd Military District command. We see its headline that it's regarding the mobilisation of RJ. That's "war units"; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: It isn't quite logical to me. It is the 11th of May. It is still the 5th Military District, so why is General Mladic drafting the order? I can see it here now. I believe he was an experienced officer and commander. As of the moment when he took up his duties, that is when he started writing orders, but the date on this one is the 11th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It is. And it comes from the 2nd Military District command; doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, the 2nd Military District. But why would then Mladic be the one drafting it? It was still Lieutenant-General Kukanjac at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Chamber has received the hand-over certificate and elements of General Mladic's personnel file. Is it really your evidence that you're not aware that General Mladic had been appointed to the 2nd Military District by the 11th of May? [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness kindly repeat his answer. We had sound problems again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you've been asked to repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I said that it is the issue of that one day. I don't know whether it was on the 11th. I know that as of the 12th the VRS came into being.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, looking again at the title, I asked you, and I don't think I got an answer, whether the reference to "RJ" refers to "war units." That's what that acronym is used for, right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, war units. That's what the RJ stands for. So order to mobilise war units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see in point 1 a description of what's going to be included in the new units, and it starts with "armed Serbian people"; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Am I supposed to -- I don't understand the question. What is it that you're asking me, the establishment of war units? The units of the 5th Corps had already been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What General Mladic is ordering is that war units be established and that armed Serbian people be included; right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I can't explain it just like that. I can't accept it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, the 5th Corps not only accepted but implemented this order; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: The order was implemented because the war units had already been established. They had their conscripts. Each conscript was assigned to a particular unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to direct your attention for the moment to the strictly confidential number 12/81-433 in the top left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask for 65 ter 32167.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an order from the 5th Corps command the next day, the 12th of May, 1992. We see at the beginning that it's issued pursuant to the order of the 2nd Military District, strictly confidential number 12/81-433 of 11 May 1992. That's the order we just looked at; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. This order was to carry out mobilisation, to arm Serb people, and to arm the volunteers who arrive and report, having previously carried out background checks for them, and to assign them to their respective units. Once in the units, they were duty-bound to follow the regulations of the unit in terms of discipline, order, security and safety, so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P7460, under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7460 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I repeated what Mr. Registrar said, I think, but you didn't ask it be -- have it admitted under seal. Mr. Registrar, is there any reason?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The only reason was that the OTP mentioned it was strictly confidential document. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the document was strictly confidential, as far as the content is concerned, at the time when it was issued. I should have asked rather than to repeat what you said, Mr. Registrar. Therefore, P7460 is admitted but as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have that back on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see that has strictly confidential number 434-4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have P7122.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an order issued by the 343rd Brigade command on the 17th of May to the Serbian Territorial Defence Staff in Prijedor, and we see at the beginning that it's issued pursuant to order strictly confidential number 434-4 of the 12th of May, 1992 issued by the 5th Corps commander. So this is an example of the functioning of the chain of command in the JNA before the transformation: The 2nd Military District issuing an order, the 5th Corps passing it down to its subordinate brigades, and in this case the 343rd Brigade passing it down to the Serbian TO staff; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was forwarded by the staff or the command of the 343rd Brigade to the TO staff. Because, by that time, the TO units had been subordinated to the JNA; in this specific case, to the 5th Corps in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P7325, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document from General Gvero on the 19th of May. We see it now bears the heading the Main Staff of the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. General Gvero describes the political situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And turning to page 2 in both languages, the second paragraph, under point II, he writes: "The state-building Serbian people living on around 65 per cent of the territory and representing around 35 per cent of the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina must fight for a total partition from the Muslim and Croatian people and must create their own state." Now, he's describing here the purpose of the war to the various corps commands, right, among other units?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Am I supposed to answer this in some way?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes. General Gvero is describing there the purpose of the war; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, here General Gvero, as the assistant commander for political affairs, is not ordering but explaining the situation as it is and as it should be. Now, whether the commanders were going to implement it in that sense was up to them, but he wasn't ordering anything here. He's providing information to the units of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to focus on my question. The information he's providing is about the purpose of the war as the Main Staff understood it; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P2874.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document dated the 21st of May, 1992 from Colonel Vukelic, and we see the header now says "1st Krajina Corps Command." And if we turn to the top of page 2 in English and the bottom of page 1 in the B/C/S, we see he's written: "The constituent Serbian people, who live on around 65 per cent of the area and represent more than 35 per cent of the population of BH, must struggle for complete separation from the Muslim and Croatian peoples and form their own state." So Colonel Vukelic has clearly received General Gvero's message about the purpose of the war; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, one can interpret it in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can we have the end of the document in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see that Colonel Vukelic at the end has written: "Inform all members of the Army of the Serbian Republic of BH about the contents of this report in the most suitable way." So this is an example of information about the purpose of the war being disseminated down from the Main Staff through the corps to the units; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what we see is the same chain of command that we saw in the previous documents from the 2nd Military District to the 5th Corps to the 343rd Brigade functioning this time from the Main Staff of the VRS to the 1st Krajina Corps to its subordinate units; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see it's a minute or two early, but I'm about to turn to a new topic and I wonder if we might take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's better then to take the break with now. Mr. Kelecevic, we would like to see you back in 20 minutes. We take a break. Therefore, we resume at 10 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear us, can you see us, at the other end of the videolink?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Testing 1, 2, 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can hear you. We can see you. Can you hear us? Can you see us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can both hear and see you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And can the representative of the Registry also hear and see us? Because it's nice to know that the witness can see and hear us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] I'm not hearing anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can the representative of the Registry now hear and see us? Apparently the witness can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we need, perhaps, technical assistance because from The Hague to the far end of the videolink, there is a two-channel connection - B/C/S and English - whereas, from what I understand there is live stream coming to The Hague. But apparently the B/C/S channel is working, the other one is not. But let me just check that again. Can the representative of the Registry still not hear us on the English channel? Apparently not.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we are trying to establish connection here with the telephone line. We seem to have lost the telephone connection momentarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that means that you can't hear us, you can't see us? No response, which seems to confirm that he cannot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since there is a fair expectation that the line will be restored within the next minute, we'll wait in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: {Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour. We can report now that we're clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's true for the B/C/S line as well?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can proceed. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Can we have 65 ter 07733.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, after the transformation of the 5th Corps into the 1st Krajina Corps, you're aware what was left of the JNA was renamed into the VJ; right? As we see here.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Mr. Traldi, we don't have the document here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the VJ continued to provide support to its former officers in the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. How do you mean, in terms of staffing or finance?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way: You and the other officers in the 1st Krajina Corps command, you continued to hold VJ posts in parallel with your VRS posts and you were paid from Belgrade; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO KELECEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. I was registered as working in Belgrade, although I was born in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the document apparently was not available to the other side. So that's at least one of the comments.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] It now is, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It now is?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I think that point one is straight-forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I just wanted to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was, of course, "as we can see," and then the answer was that they couldn't see it. Now having looked at the document, Witness, does that change in any way the answer you gave earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. From what I can see, no. I was still a staff member of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you were on your feet --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a second ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think the question was dealing with the 5th Corps, and the 5th Corps was renamed. But here in this document, we see that JNA was renamed into VJ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think Mr. Lukic may be very politely suggesting that I was misrecorded on the transcript to have asked whether the 5th Corps was renamed into the VJ when I had asked whether the JNA was renamed into the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I think, Mr. Lukic, apart from that, and also the witness in his answer I think sufficiently explained what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7461. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Witness, you said a second ago: "No, not at all." What did you mean to say by that? That it wasn't the 5th Corps that was renamed or that it was not the JNA that was renamed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 5th Corps was just renamed into 2nd Corps and remained the 2nd Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the JNA was renamed Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The JNA would later be renamed. It wasn't renamed at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
